title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1970-02-11
lineage: Akai GX636 direct tape head output  > Bottlehead tube tape pre w/a pair of Tesla tubes circa 1960  > Apogee Mini Me 24/96  > Apogee Mini DAC monitoring and mastering  > FLAC
source: SBD MR Technics RS 1506 @7.5 ips > Revox A77(Bob Menke)@7.5 ips > Revox A77(Pat Lee)@7.5 ips

ai_review.summary: High‑energy Spanish Jam and lively Lovelight shine on this solid soundboard capture, though the tape cuts off abruptly before Shine On Me.
ai_review.review: The performance is a wild, busy tapestry of improvisation – a scorching Spanish Jam that even features Peter Green‑ish notes, followed by an unexpectedly cool Greg Allman‑led Lovelight with Pigpen egging everyone on and Phil’s bass line driving the groove. The recording sounds clear and well‑balanced (typical soundboard quality) but ends abruptly before "Shine On Me," leaving the set incomplete.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviewers consistently praise the musical flow and standout jams, while noting only a minor recording flaw (abrupt ending).

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear and balanced overall; however the tape ends abruptly before "Shine On Me," indicating a cut in the source.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A densely packed, high‑energy second half with a busy Spanish Jam that segues into Lovelight, highlighted by Pigpen’s vocal fire‑starter and Phil’s driving bass line.

band_member_comments.Phil: His bass line in the Spanish Jam is noted as a key element of the jam.
